messages:
mina: Hey everyone, quick question on secrets approvals. I submitted a Vault request for a Stripe test key and included the app owner, but the form says we also need a security approver. Who should I @mention and is there a faster path for low-risk dev/stage keys?
ana: Welcome @mina! For dev/stage you can tag the app owner + devex and mark env=dev to get expedited review. Security approval is required for prod. If you mark the request as CI or pipeline usage include the pipeline identity.
mina: Good to know. What if we need emergency access during an incident? How does oncall get a quick temp credential?
sre-oncall: Oncall can use the break-glass flow in the secrets runbook. Request a temporary role via the ops portal which creates a 1h Vault role with audit logging. Must include incident ID and get a one-time secops ack.
devex-bot: Request SR-2026-777 has been created and queued for review. Tracker: https://redwood-internal/requests/SR-2026-777
secops: If you expect to need emergency oncall access regularly, add an "oncall-access" note in the request so we pre-authorize the escalation path. Also include rotation cadence and who owns rotation.
mina: For local dev, should I put test keys in my keychain or use Vault dev tokens?
ana: Use Vault dev tokens or the Vault agent with a dev role. If you must persist a secret locally, use the OS keychain and mark it dev-only. Never commit any keys to git.
mina: Thanks all 60a submitting with the oncall note now. Appreciate the help!
